en: In the early twentieth century, Japanese official, academic, and commercial publications deployed texts, pictures, and maps to manufacture the “large reservoir of cultural imaginaries”

that have reemerged as reference points and resources for Taiwan’s indigenous renaissance in the twenty-first century. In what began as a quest to wrest resources, impose administrative order, and promote immigration to an erstwhile Qing borderland in the late 1890s and 1900s, Japan’s colonial administration, tourism industry, and scholarly apparatus, by the 1930s, had completed numerous projects in ethnic typification, geobody construction, and racialization to institutionalize indigeneity in Taiwan. This concluding chapter analyzes these three interrelated processes to demonstrate how the increased intensity of resource extraction in colonial Taiwan intersected with historical trends in reprographic technology and new forms of state making to ethnically pluralize the island’s populations under the umbrella of an Aborigine Territory.
zh: 20世纪初，日本的官方、学术与商业出版物运用文字、图片和地图，制造出“庞大的文化想象资源库”

，其中的材料在21世纪重新受到重视，成为台湾原住民复兴运动的参照点与资源。19世纪90年代末至20世纪头十年，日本对这片昔日清朝边地的行动，起初只是为了攫取资源、强行建立行政秩序并推动移民；到20世纪30年代，日本的殖民行政机构、旅游业与学术体制已完成众多族群类型化、地理体建构与种族化的工程，从而在台湾将原住民性制度化。本书最后一章分析这三个相互关联的过程，以说明殖民台湾资源开采强度的不断加深，如何与图文复制技术的发展和国家建构的新形式相汇合，从而在“蕃地”这一行政框架下把岛上人口划为多个族群。

en: THE GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION AS THE AGE OF ANTHROPOLOGICAL TYPIFICATION
zh: 作为人类学类型化时代的全球转型

en: …[I]n premodern European discourses, non-Western peoples tend to be characterized not in any anthropologically specific terms, but as a lack or poorer form of the values of the centre.... My analytical fiction... [postulates]... a shift from an absence of “the Other” (as a being accorded any singular character) to a worldview that imagines a plurality of different races or peoples. The distinctively modern and anthropological [discourse] projects natural differences among people that may be rendered at one time as different “nations,” at another as distinct “races” or “cultures.” The underlying epistemic operation —of partitioning the human species—makes possible a variety of political and ethnographic projects: particular populations may be visible as objects of government; they may serve as ethnological illustrations or subversive counter-examples in comparative social argument; and these reified characters may be available for appropriation in anti-colonialist, nationalist narratives.
zh: ……在前现代欧洲话语中，非西方民族往往不是按各自具体的人类学特征来描述，而是被说成缺少中心社会的价值，或只以较差的方式体现了那些价值……我的分析性虚构……[假定]……一种转变：从“他者”的缺席（即被认为有自身独特性的人群），转向一种想象出多种不同种族或民族的世界观。这种独具现代性与人类学色彩的[话语]把人群之间的差异描绘成天然的，这些差异有时被表述为不同的“民族”，有时又被表述为各异的“种族”或“文化”。其底层的认识论操作——对人类物种加以分割——使各种政治与民族志工程成为可能：特定人群可作为治理对象而变得可见；他们可在比较社会论争中充当民族学例证或颠覆性的反例；而这些被当作固定实体的特征，又可供反殖民主义、民族主义叙事挪用。

en: In his definition of pluralism, or anthropological typification, Nicholas Thomas argues that modern colonial epistemology “partitions” subject populations into internally cohesive, distinctive, ontologically stable groups whose unique traits are embodied in representative figures, or anthropological types. To put these modern anthropological paradigms into relief, Thomas defines premodern ethnology as its foil, in terms strikingly similar to the assessment of Qing ethnology by Japanese ethnographer Inō Kanori. For Thomas, anthropology’s interest in the languages, technologies, and belief systems of remote and small populations reflects, in part, modern cultural pluralism’s axiom that all peoples are inherently worthy as members of the human race. Pluralism represents an epistemic rupture from Christian and Enlightenment paradigms of incorporation/assimilation, argues Thomas. This is so because difference configured plurally has something to offer multiple constituencies, as it gains traction as the object of scientific inquiry, exotic interest, ethnic pride, or racialist pessimism. In the new dispensation, pluralism is invested with an emotional intensity that forestalls the withering away of diverse cultural formations under the impact of the homogenizing forces consolidated during the long nineteenth century’s global transformation (see introduction).
zh: 在对多元主义（或曰人类学类型化）的定义中，尼古拉斯·托马斯主张，现代殖民认识论将臣属人群“分割”为内部凝聚、彼此有别、被认为本质稳定的群体，其独特性状体现在代表性人物亦即人类学类型之中。为凸显这些现代人类学范式，托马斯把前现代民族学界定为其对照面，所用的措辞与日本民族学家伊能嘉矩对清代民族学的评估惊人地相似。在托马斯看来，人类学对居住偏远、人口较少的群体的语言、技术与信仰体系的兴趣，部分反映了现代文化多元主义的一条公理：所有民族作为人类成员都天生具有价值。托马斯主张，多元主义代表着与基督教及启蒙运动的纳入／同化范式之间的一次认识论断裂。之所以如此，是因为把差异理解为多种文化形态并存，可以回应不同群体的需要——它作为科学探究、猎奇兴趣、族群自豪或基于种族观的悲观论的对象而获得影响力。在这一新格局中，多元主义被注入了一种情感强度，从而阻止了多样文化形态在漫长的19世纪全球转型期间凝聚起来的同质化力量冲击下走向消亡（见导论）。

en: For Meiji ethnologists, who defined themselves as pluralists in Thomas’s sense of the word, the first Chinese travelers to Taiwan were the very picture of premodern traveler/anthropologists. They postulated an intellectual chasm between themselves and their Qing predecessors in terms not unlike the ones Thomas uses to separate premodern and modern anthropological imaginaries. For example, in 1905, a decade into Japanese colonial rule in Taiwan, Inō wrote:
zh: 对于明治时期的民族学家而言——他们可视为托马斯所说的多元主义者——最早到台湾的中国旅行者正是前现代旅行者／人类学家的典型写照。他们假定自己与清代前辈之间存在一道知识上的鸿沟，所用的措辞与托马斯用来区分前现代与现代人类学想象的措辞不无相似。例如，1905年，即日本殖民统治台湾十年之际，伊能写道：

en: When the Chinese first learned of Taiwan’s location, they acknowledged the existence of the island’s own people, or “the natives.”...But at the time, they only recognized the natives as a different people, with different language and customs, but did not give them a particular name.... ... They did not, [however,] make observations about race.
zh: 当中国人最初得知台湾的位置时，他们承认岛上自有其居民，即“土著”。……但当时，他们只是把土著视为语言与风俗不同的另一群人，却未给他们一个特定的名称。……明代时，使用的是“东番”（dongfan）这一名称。……清朝占据台湾后，依据政治上是否归顺，分为两大类，即“生番”与“熟番”……[然而，]他们并未对种族加以观察。

en: As the Qing period wore on, Inō wrote, Chinese observers began to add details to their reports and make distinctions among the various non-Han peoples of Taiwan. They even propounded theories for the origins of the Taiwanese natives. But in the final analysis, the “Chinese observations about the Taiwanese natives’ essential nature, in relation to race, were extremely crude. There are no theories propounded here worthy of reference in scholarly discourse. The reason for this can be attributed to one cause: they based their theories on a general view that recognized the natives as beyond the pale of civilization, almost as a different species, one largely excluded from humanity.”
zh: 伊能写道，随着清代时光推移，中国观察者开始在其记述中增添细节，并对台湾各非汉人群加以区分。他们甚至提出了关于台湾土著起源的种种理论。但归根结底，“中国人从种族角度就台湾土著的本质所作的观察极其粗陋。这里提出的理论没有一条值得在学术论述中援引。其原因可归于一端：他们的理论建立在一种总体看法之上，即把土著视为处于文明藩篱之外，几乎当作另一物种，仿佛他们基本不属于人类。”

en: It is clear from this passage that by “race,” Inō meant something more than a bundle of genetic traits that defined a Mendelian population, biologically or somatically. While Inō’s project, as we shall see, essentialized and homogenized each subgroup of indigenous people through the process of typification, it also vindicated their humanity.
zh: 从这段话可以清楚看出，伊能所说的“种族”，含义不止于生物学或体质上界定一个孟德尔式种群的一组遗传性状。正如我们将看到的，伊能的工程虽通过类型化过程将原住民的每一亚群本质化、同质化，却也为承认他们同属人类作了辩护。

en: Thomas rightly insists that modern colonizers were far from unified in their conceptions of populations that underwent “anthropological typification.” For Thomas, typification could shade into a version of relativism. Preservationist ethnologists or missionaries, in some cases, attempted to militate against the necropolitical Darwinian outlook of their fellow colonialists. In our case, Gotō Shinpei’s point man on aborigine policy, Mochiji Rokusaburō, wears the black hat. In the face of their exculpatory discourse, Mochiji excoriated anthropologists for their relatively positive assessments of indigenes. In Mochiji’s view, there were only two kinds of “savages”: compliant and rebellious. The rebels existed beyond the bounds of sovereignty. Mochiji had little patience with pluralists and implicitly blamed them for Japan’s lack of industrial progress in the uplands.
zh: 托马斯正确地坚持认为，现代殖民者对于经历“人类学类型化”的人群，其观念远非一致。在托马斯看来，类型化可能渐变为某种相对主义。主张保存当地文化的民族学家或传教士，在某些情况下试图抵制其殖民同僚那种死亡政治式的达尔文主义观念。在我们的案例中，后藤新平在理蕃政策上的干将持地六三郎代表了后一种立场。面对为原住民辩护的论述，持地痛斥人类学家对原住民相对正面的评价。在持地看来，“蕃人”只有两种：顺从的与叛逆的。叛逆者存在于主权边界之外。持地对多元主义者毫无耐心，并含蓄地把日本在山地上缺乏工业进展归咎于他们。

en: MEIJI NATIONALISM AND GEOBODY CONSTRUCTION IN COLONIAL TAIWAN
zh: 明治民族主义与殖民台湾的地理体建构

en: For Thomas, “colonialism’s culture” locates positivities (“cultures”) among the “ungoverned,” “undergoverned,” or “savage” peoples who are the objects of commercial, missionary, or military forces in the expanding international system. In contrast, early modern ecclesiastical/dynastic agents in such areas posited a negativity, or an absence of attributes thought to be constitutive of the imperial center, in their accounts of “barbarians/savages.”

In this analysis, Taiwan’s solidly colored secondary geobodies became placeholders for the positivities, or cultures, that displaced the blank, absent spaces of “savagery” in the Qing imaginary. The maps in
–34 illustrate a sequence of contrasting logics.
zh: 在托马斯看来，“殖民主义的文化”在处于“未受治理”“治理不足”或所谓“野蛮”状态的人群中，辨认出这些群体自身的“文化”，他们正是扩张中的国际体系里商业、传教或军事力量所作用的对象。相比之下，近代早期在这些地区活动的教会／王朝代理人，则在其关于“蛮夷／番人”的记述中设定了一种否定性，即缺失那些被认为构成帝国中心之属性的特征。
在这一分析中，台湾那些以实色填充的二阶地理体，成了这些群体各有自身文化的标志，取代了清代想象中“野蛮”所留下的空白、缺席的空间。

en: The map in

is taken from an 1895 Japanese commercial publication; it is based on Western maps of Taiwan from the treaty-port era. In it, Taiwan is bifurcated into an eastern “savage” half and a western “Chinese” zone. The line separating the two zones is two-dimensional, stark and clear. This cartographic convention, which does not demarcate administrative boundaries or conform to natural land forms or emic senses of place but is rather a purely ideological construction, replicates the discourse on “separate Taiwans” advocated by Charles LeGendre after 1872 (see chapter 1).

In LeGendre’s view, over half of Taiwan lacked government and civility. These maps, in fact, made the argument that over half of Taiwan was terra nullius, and up for grabs in terms of international law.
zh: 的地图取自1895年的一部日本商业出版物；它以通商口岸时代西方绘制的台湾地图为底本。图中，台湾被一分为二：东半部是“蕃人”区，西半部是“中国人”区。分隔两区的那条线平铺在地图上，鲜明而清晰。这一制图惯例既不标示行政边界，也不依循自然地貌，也不反映当地人的地方观念，而纯粹是一种意识形态建构，它复制了李仙得在1872年后所鼓吹的“两个台湾”话语（见第1章）。
在李仙得看来，台湾有一半以上没有政府管辖，也没有他所认可的文明秩序。这些地图实际上提出了这样的论点：台湾有一半以上是无主地（terra nullius），依国际法可任人攫取。

en: The extension of Thongchai’s geobody concept to second-order geobodies is justifiable, I think, because indigenous-territory geobodies within geobodies, like national geobodies, were strategic responses to the era’s competitive imperialism. In each case, cartography was fundamentally about the mastery of space from a remote, central location at a bureaucratic apex. Whereas late nineteenth century Thai monarchs adapted an alien form of cartography to preserve autonomy in the face of an encroaching international system, the Japanese anthropologists in our story sketched their ethnic maps to extrapolate knowledge gained in limited and specific encounters to assert mastery over territories whose state of lawlessness and opacity was perceived as detrimental to the survival of the Japanese Empire.
zh: 我认为，把通猜（Thongchai）的地理体概念延伸到二阶地理体是站得住脚的，因为地理体之内的原住民领地地理体，与国家地理体一样，都是对那个时代竞争性帝国主义的战略回应。在每一种情形中，制图从根本上都是为了从远离当地、居于官僚体系最高层的权力中心掌控空间。19世纪晚期的泰国君主面对不断进逼的国际体系，采纳了一种外来的制图形式以维护自主；而我们故事中的日本人类学家绘制族群地图，则是把在有限而具体的接触中获得的知识加以外推，以宣示对那些领地的掌控——这些地区被认为缺乏法律秩序、实情难明，因而威胁日本帝国的存续。

en: THE GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION AS THE AGE OF RACE
zh: 作为种族时代的全球转型

en: As self-aware non-Westerners, Japanese imperialists are said to have practiced a sort of mimesis as they internalized and reapplied race as a discursive weapon vis-à-vis other Asians, or to have refracted Western idioms in the process of becoming a full-blown colonial power. This narrative of Japanese race making as one of mimesis and/or refraction focuses our attention on the question of how race was “domesticated by the Japanese” and then redeployed in the colonies.

As we shall see, the mimetic framework is not without value for the study of race making in colonial Taiwan. Indeed, formally trained and westward-facing ethnologists like Inō Kanori, Torii Ryūzō, and Mori Ushinosuke had a role to play in the popularization, operationalization, and conceptualization of indigenes as members of a distinct race or races. They truly exhibited the processes of mimesis and refraction, so to speak. But their formulations were mediated, modified, and contested in the mass media by metropolitan visionaries, postcard publishers, editorialist-constables, colonized subjects themselves, and myriad others who were at best loosely affiliated with explicit programs of civilization and enlightenment or Westernization.
zh: 作为具有自我意识的非西方人，据说日本帝国主义者实践了某种摹仿：他们把种族观念内化并重新用作针对其他亚洲人的话语武器；或者说，他们在成为成熟的殖民强国的过程中，对西方的表达方式加以改造。这种把日本种族建构视为摹仿和／或折射的叙事，把我们的注意力集中于这样一个问题：种族如何被“日本人驯化”，继而在殖民地重新部署。

正如我们将看到的，摹仿框架对于研究殖民台湾的种族建构并非没有价值。的确，像伊能嘉矩、鸟居龙藏、森丑之助这样受过正规训练、面向西方的民族学家，不但把原住民概念化为一个或多个独立种族，还推动了这些观念的传播和实际应用。可以说，他们确实展现了摹仿与折射的过程。但他们的表述在大众媒体中被日本本土的倡议者、明信片出版商、兼任社论作者的警察、被殖民者自身以及无数其他人加以转述、改写或质疑，而这些人至多只是松散地附属于文明开化或西化的明确纲领。

en: Moreover, the Qing precedents in aborigine administration, image production, and category construction, all of which deeply informed Japanese projects in race making, fell largely outside the history of Euro-American cultural history. In light of race’s multiple and independently accreted genealogies, then, the single-origin, diffusionist model of race as subfield of European intellectual history is of limited utility for a long-term analysis of indigenous Taiwan’s encounter with the global transformation.
zh: 此外，清代在番人行政、图像生产与范畴建构方面的先例——所有这些都深刻影响了日本的种族建构工程——大体上并非源自欧美文化的历史。因此，鉴于种族具有多重且各自独立形成的谱系，把种族视为欧洲思想史一个分支的单一起源、传播论模型，对于长期分析原住民台湾与全球转型的遭遇，用处有限。

en: In light of these considerations, this chapter will adopt a looser construction of “race” as a category and social force. Following W. J. T. Mitchell, I regard race as a “medium,” akin to a language game, rather than as a Euro-American pseudoscientific category that creates its own referent. Mitchell has argued that the medium of race provides the iconography and language for representing

theory, ideal, or argument that asserts the internal homogeneity and “groupness” of particular “kinds” of human beings and their distinctiveness from similarly configured groups (races). Mitchell’s conceptualization recalls Thomas’s definition of typification/pluralism, insofar as it minimizes the difference between “culture” and “species” as bases of invidious comparison. But it goes further. Mitchell concedes that the racial medium is often inflected with the familiar metaphor of species difference. But “race talk and race thinking” can also adopt the imagery and discourse of culture, class, status, or gender to configure difference as natural.

Mitchell’s capacious definition is salient here because, as we shall see, photographer-anthropologists, publishers, propagandists, and merchants rarely portrayed Taiwanese racial difference in strict, Linnaean terms or even in logically consistent language or iconography. Rather, race was the thread or mediating category that conjoined a mix of ethnonyms, slurs, stereotypes, and ideals into a language of difference and hierarchy.
zh: 基于这些考虑，本章将对作为范畴与社会力量的“种族”采取一种较宽松的理解。追随米切尔（W. J. T. Mitchell），我把种族视为一种“媒介”，类似于一种语言游戏，而非一个生产出自己所指对象的欧美伪科学范畴。米切尔主张，种族这一媒介提供了一整套图像与语言，用以表征任何断言特定“种类”人类内部同质性与“群体性”、并断言其有别于同样配置的其他群体（种族）的理论、理想或论证。米切尔的概念化令人想起托马斯对类型化／多元主义的定义，因为它把“文化”与“物种”作为歧视性比较之基础的差别最小化了。但它走得更远。米切尔承认，种族媒介常常带有人们熟悉的物种差异隐喻的色彩。但“种族言谈与种族思维”也可以采纳文化、阶级、地位或性别的意象与话语，使这些差异看起来是天然的。
米切尔这一宽泛的定义在此尤为切题，因为正如我们将看到的，摄影师兼人类学家、出版商、宣传家与商人很少以严格的林奈式措辞、甚至很少使用逻辑一致的语言或图像体系来描绘台湾的种族差异。相反，种族是一条线索或中介范畴，把族名、蔑称、刻板印象与理想混合起来，编织成一种差异与等级的语言。

en: Mitchell, along with a number of other analysts, including Patrick Wolfe, considers modern formulations of race to be the aftereffects and not the cause of racism. In other words, racism is “what hurts.” Racism is the practice of discrimination, genocide, exclusion, isolation, or segregation implemented against a race.

Qing-period (1700s–1895) resource wars along the frontier of Han settlement on the island of Taiwan produced a racism whose institutionalization provided the terminology and raw materials for Japanese race scientists to contend with in the Meiji period and beyond.

Therefore, the use of imported Western ideas involving somatological or linguistic criteria for racial classification did not produce racism in Taiwan but did provide a new language game, or medium, for framing policy options that could exacerbate or mitigate preexisting forms of racism.
zh: 米切尔与包括帕特里克·沃尔夫（Patrick Wolfe）在内的若干研究者一样，认为现代的种族表述是种族主义的后果而非原因。换言之，种族主义才是“造成伤害的东西”。种族主义是针对某一种族实施的歧视、种族灭绝、排斥、隔离或分隔的实践。
清代（18世纪至1895年）台湾岛上汉人垦殖前沿的资源战争，产生了一种种族主义，其制度化为此后明治时期及更晚的日本种族科学家提供了必须应对的术语与原材料。
因此，采用从西方引进以体质或语言为依据的种族分类观念，并未在台湾制造出种族主义，却提供了一种新的语言游戏或媒介，用以框定那些可能加剧或缓解既有种族主义形态的政策选项。

en: To understand the genesis, meaning, and staying power of ethnically pluralist, biologically invidious, and territorially bounded indigenous formations in Taiwan, we must not only ask what men like Gotō Shinpei hoped to achieve by institutionalizing the scientifically accredited notions of hierarchy and order imbibed during his study of medicine in Germany. We must also identify and locate the dispersed interests, mechanisms, and micropolitical arrangements that allowed the medium of race to proliferate and sustain itself across vast social fields.
The power of anthropology and its related discourses is not to be found in connections between individual ethnologists and particular policies but rather in the rupture it introduced into discourse.
zh: 要理解台湾那些按族群区分、以生物学划分优劣且在领土上有明确边界的原住民群体的起源、意义与持久力，我们不仅必须追问：像后藤新平这样的人，把他在德国学医期间汲取的、有科学权威为其背书的等级与秩序观念加以制度化，究竟希望达成什么。我们还必须识别并定位那些分散的利益、机制与微观政治安排，正是它们使种族这一媒介得以在广阔的社会场域中扩散并自我维系。
人类学及其相关话语的力量，不在于个别民族学家与特定政策之间的联系，而在于它带来的话语转折。

en: As the following sections will illustrate, even if few Japanese or Taiwanese read ethnological reports emanating from the highlands in the early twentieth century, ethnology reflected and inspired a plethora of lithographs, line drawings, paintings, ethnic maps, and photographs of indigenes. These artifacts circulated via newspapers, picture postcards, photo magazines, museum exhibitions, and exposition guides from the onset of colonial rule in 1895 right down to the end of the Pacific War in 1945. By the 1930s at the latest, it would have been impossible for tourists, colonial administrators, or politically conscious Japanese citizens to imagine a Taiwan shorn of its indigenous presence. Despite their relatively small numbers, about 2 percent of the island’s population, the Indigenous Peoples produced by Japanese graphic artists, novelists, administrators, scholars, and the indigenes they interviewed, conducted trade with, photographed, and married covered half of the island’s surface. The Atayal, Sediq, Truku, Bunun, Paiwan, Ami, Yami, Saisiyat, Rukai, and Tsou peoples were officially, academically, and popularly understood to be Taiwan’s original inhabitants and were composed of several contiguous but distinct culture zones—in an interwar milieu that saw the conqueror’s right to rule displaced by the discourse on sovereignty and authenticity.
zh: 正如以下各节将说明的，即便20世纪初几乎没有日本人或台湾人阅读那些出自关于山地的民族学报告，民族学仍与大量原住民题材的图像相互影响，其中包括石版画、线描、绘画、族群地图与照片。从1895年殖民统治伊始直到1945年太平洋战争结束，这些制品经由报纸、图画明信片、摄影杂志、博物馆展览与博览会指南流通。最迟到20世纪30年代，游客、殖民行政官员或有政治意识的日本公民，已不可能想象一个没有原住民的台湾。尽管人数相对稀少——约占全岛人口的2%——经日本平面艺术家、小说家、行政官员、学者，以及同他们交谈、交易、接受拍摄或通婚的原住民共同塑造，原住民族群在当时的表述中占据了全岛一半的面积。泰雅、赛德克、德路固、布农、排湾、阿美、雅美、赛夏、鲁凯与邹族，在官方、学术与大众层面都被理解为台湾的原初居民，由若干彼此相连却又各异的文化区构成——而在两次大战之间的那个环境中，基于征服者统治权的论述，已让位于以主权和本真性为中心的论述。

en: The affirmation of indigenous autochthony and ethnic integrity was much more than the discovery of truths obscured by Sinocentric Qing discourse. As a broad-based repudiation of the notion that Taiwan’s interior and eastern rift valley were inhabited by peoples “beyond the pale” (Thomas’s “poorer version of the values at the center”), the creation of indigenous geobodies in Taiwan was, dialectically speaking, the negation of a negation. That is to say, the indigenous geobodies that coalesced in 1920s Taiwan did not restore Indigenous Peoples to their rightful place as original owners of the island, but rather witnessed the birth of two-way symbolic traffic between a nationalized citizenry and an excluded minority that operated, for the first time, without a mediating layer of brokers such as Kondō the Barbarian, Pan Bunkiet, or Watan Yūra. This new configuration, which I have referred to as “indigenous modernity” in chapter 3, describes an international system of nation-states riddled with pockets of quasi sovereignty. This order is sustained by the persistent and even heroic efforts of indigenes to reclaim ancestral lands and maintain corporate identities in the face of detribalization and assimilation movements. As currently configured, it also requires indigenes to perform identities in ways consistent with the aspirations, fantasies, and expectations of settler/majority populations who still control most levers of state power.
zh: 对原住民本土起源与族群完整性的确认，远不止是发现了被中华中心的清代话语所遮蔽的真相。作为对“台湾内陆与东部纵谷居住着‘化外之民’（托马斯所说的‘中心价值的较劣版本’）”这一观念的广泛否定，台湾原住民地理体的创造，用辩证法的话说，是一次否定之否定。也就是说，1920年代在台湾凝聚成形的原住民地理体，并未把原住民恢复到其作为岛屿原初所有者的正当地位，而是见证了一种双向符号交往的诞生——它在一个被国民化的公民群体与一个被排斥的少数群体之间展开，并且首次不再需要“生番近藤”、潘文杰或瓦丹有洛这类掮客作为中介层。这一新构形，即我在第3章中所称的“原住民现代性”，描述的是一个布满准主权飞地的民族国家国际体系。这一秩序得以维系，靠的是原住民面对去部落化与同化运动时，为收复祖地、维持作为群体的身份而作的持续乃至英勇的努力。就目前的配置而言，它还要求原住民以符合那些仍掌控着大部分国家权力杠杆的定居殖民者及其后代构成的多数群体的渴望、幻想与期待的方式，来展演身份。

en: UENO SEN’ICHI AND THE PREHISTORY OF GEOBODY CONSTRUCTION IN TAIWAN
zh: 上野专一与台湾地理体建构的史前史

en: The Taiwan Government-General set up its Taipei administration in June 1895. Even before officials could safely report for duty, publications about the curious folkways of the empire’s new subjects began to circulate in Japan. Especially prominent were travel accounts of hill peoples, collectively known by terms that are variations on the theme “savage,” such as
, or

Takigawa Miyotarō’s Shinryōchi Taiwantō (Our new territory: The island of Taiwan, published in June 1895) was typical in one respect: it recycled the report of Ministry of Foreign Affairs staffer Ueno Sen’ichi, who visited Taiwan in 1881 and 1891.

Ueno’s report, which was introduced briefly in chapter 1, is an amalgam of Ueno’s firsthand observations, smatterings of cribbed material, and Ueno’s translations of British Imperial Maritime Customs agent George Taylor’s notes on ethnography.

In addition to cropping up as source material for commercial publications, Ueno’s notes on Taiwan were widely disseminated within Japan’s military apparatus. Thus, we can assume they had been combed over by any Japanese official, soldier, or civilian with a position of responsibility in Taiwan in the post-1895 period.
zh: 台湾总督府于1895年6月在台北设立行政机构。早在官员们能够安全到任之前，关于帝国新臣民奇特风俗的出版物便已开始在日本流通。尤为突出的是关于山地民族的游记，这些民族被统称为“蕃人”一类称呼的不同变体，如蕃人（banjin）、生蕃人（seibanjin）、野蛮人（yabanjin）或蕃族（banzoku）。
泷川宫太郎（Takigawa Miyotarō）的《新领地台湾岛》（Shinryōchi Taiwantō，1895年6月出版）在一个方面颇具典型性：它沿用了外务省职员上野专一的报告，上野曾于1881年和1891年访问台湾。
上野的报告在第1章已简要介绍，它是上野的第一手观察、零星抄袭材料以及上野对英籍海关关员乔治·泰勒（George Taylor）民族志笔记之翻译的混合体。
除了作为商业出版物的素材来源出现外，上野关于台湾的笔记还在日本军事机器内部广泛传播。因此，我们可以假定，1895年后在台湾担任要职的日本官员、军人或文职人员，都已把它们翻检过一遍。

en: Ueno began with a discussion of Qing data and classification, continued with a digest of George Taylor’s observations, and concluded with his 1891 travelogue of a visit to the environs of Quchi, home of several prominent Atayal players in the construction of indigenous modernity. To orient Japanese readers, Ueno referenced the term “eighteen tribes of Langqiao.” He reminded readers that this familiar sobriquet applied only to southern Taiwanese and that there were many more than eighteen tribes, even in Hengchun. According to an 1879 Qing census of the area, wrote Ueno, there were some fifty-eight villages under the jurisdiction of Hengchun, plus another forty-six villages of the “Puyuma race” (
), who also lived in Hengchun district.
zh: 上野先讨论清代的数据与分类，接着摘要介绍乔治·泰勒的观察，最后以他1891年走访屈尺一带的游记作结——屈尺是若干在原住民现代性建构中扮演重要角色的泰雅人的家乡。为帮助日本读者理解当地情况，上野援引了“琅峤十八社”这一说法。他提醒读者，这个熟悉的称呼只指台湾南部的一部分居民，而且即便在恒春，部落也远不止十八个。上野写道，据1879年清代对该地区的一次人口普查，恒春辖下约有五十八个村社，此外还有四十六个“卑南族”（shuzoku）村社，他们也住在恒春辖境。

en: Ueno’s updates supplemented a voluminous body of Japanese records from the 1874 invasion. Much had changed in Hengchun as a result of Shen Baozhen’s “open the mountains, pacify the barbarians” policies of the post-1874 period. This updated baseline data was presumably useful to Japanese constables and soldiers who fanned out across Taiwan in 1895 and 1896 to set up the rudiments of rural administration. In a less practical vein, Ueno’s report also provided a somewhat confused digest of existing ethnographic information. Ueno wrote that all of Taiwan’s so-called
(raw aborigines) could be subdivided into four ethnic groups/races (

): the Paiwan, Zhiben (Depon), Amis, and Pingpu (Pepo). This taxonomy, inherited from Taylor, left out much of the island’s indigenous population and presented some logical inconsistencies. For one, Ueno subsumed the Plains-dwelling tribes (
) under the rubric
. In contrast, later systems considered
to be synonymous with
, a category defined antithetically to

. Like his crude taxonomic scheme, Ueno’s descriptions of origin myths followed Taylor verbatim. Taylor himself relied upon oral testimony and legends to fix ancient indigenous migration routes to Taiwan, instead of having recourse to comparative linguistic data or the maps of the global distribution of cultural traits preferred by academic ethnologists of the time. For all of its problems, this shaky overview formed the baseline for Japanese ethnologists. The “four to five different tribes of
discovered by European writers” mentioned in Inō’s 1895 manifesto refer to Taylor’s classification, while Torii Ryūzō’s early classificatory work also cites Taylor as a pioneer.
zh: 上野增补的资料补充了1874年侵台以来卷帙浩繁的日本记录。由于沈葆桢在1874年后推行“开山抚番”政策，恒春已发生很大变化。这些更新过的基础资料，想必对1895至1896年间分散到台湾各地、着手建立乡村行政雏形的日本警察与军人颇有用处。在不那么实用的方面，上野的报告还对既有民族志信息作了一份略显混乱的摘要。上野写道，台湾所有所谓的生番（shengfan）都可细分为四个族群／种族（shuzoku）：排湾、知本（Depon）、阿美与平埔（Pepo）。这一承袭自泰勒的分类法，漏掉了岛上大部分原住民人口，且存在一些逻辑上的不一致。例如，上野把居住平原的部落（pingpu-zu，平埔族）归入生番这一名目之下。相比之下，后来的分类体系认为平埔族与“熟蕃”同义，且把“熟蕃”界定为与“生蕃”相对的类别。与其粗陋的分类方案一样，上野对起源神话的描述也逐字照搬泰勒。泰勒本人依靠口述证词与传说来确定古代原住民迁台的路线，而非借助比较语言学数据，或当时学院民族学家偏好的文化特质全球分布图。尽管问题重重，日本民族学家仍以这份并不可靠的概述为出发点。伊能1895年宣言中提到的“欧洲作者发现的四到五个不同的生番部落”，指的就是泰勒的分类；而鸟居龙藏早期的分类工作也把泰勒引为先驱。

en: Ueno’s report described the costume, ornaments, and physical appearance of his Atayal interlocutors but did not hazard to classify indigenes into subgroups—he instead used the Chinese term

(savage). As we saw in chapter 2, Ueno’s report focused instead on the cultural practices that facilitated communication between Atayal people and outsiders, to serve as a practical guide for the conduct of business. Thus, the material items it assiduously described—tobacco, glass beads, red-dyed cloth, bottled spirits—were not evidence of autochthony or cultural integrity but rather were elements of a hybrid material repertoire that had sprung up between the economically interdependent but politically independent peoples on each side of Taiwan’s “savage border.”
zh: 上野的报告描述了他那些泰雅对话者的服饰、饰物与体貌，却不敢贸然把原住民细分为亚群——他转而使用汉语词“番人”（fanren）。正如我们在第2章所见，上野的报告反而聚焦于那些促进泰雅人与外人沟通的文化实践，以充当与当地人交涉的实用指南。因此，报告不厌其详地记下的物品——烟草、玻璃珠、染红的布、瓶装烈酒——并非本土起源或文化完整性的证据，而是双方共有的一套混合物质文化的一部分。这套物质文化在台湾“生番界”两侧那些经济上相互依赖、政治上各自独立的民族之间应运而生。

en: THE TAIWAN GOVERNMENT-GENERAL’S FIRST ENCOUNTER WITH INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
zh: 台湾总督府与原住民的首次接触

en: The newly ensconced Taiwan Government-General’s first official mission to Dakekan-area Atayal peoples followed Ueno’s gifting and drinking playbook, some two decades later. Mori Ushinosuke classified the Atayal members of this mission as the cismontane Dakekan tribes (
). In the early 1900s, this group consisted of nine settlements.
Jiaobanshan was the largest of these.
zh: 大约二十年后，刚刚设立的台湾总督府首次派官方使团与大嵙崁一带的泰雅人接触时，沿用了上野以赠礼和共饮展开交涉的做法。森丑之助把这次交涉中的泰雅代表归类为前大嵙崁蕃（mae-Taikokan-ban，山前大嵙崁部落）。20世纪初，这一群体由九个聚落组成。
角板山是其中最大的一个。

en: The Japanese press and colonial bureaucracy generated at least seven written reports of the events bounded by Captain Watanabe’s August 29 exploratory meeting near the Dakekan garrison and the return home of the Jiaobanshan delegation on September 12. Contemporary imagery derived from the embassy suggests that Japanese officials, writers, and publishers did not bring ethnologically informed, pluralistic categories with them to Taiwan in 1895. These would be formulated and disseminated over the course of colonial rule, on site. For example, articulate officials like Hashiguchi Bunzō and Captain Hirano Akio employed Qing terminology for “savagery” (
) and mentioned specific settlements and the names of their leaders. They did not, however, use the term

. Nor did they attach culture zones to ethnic maps of the island. As we shall see, the first wave of Japanese-produced icons of indigeneity in Taiwan conform to Thomas’s ideal-typical premodern imaginary, wherein other peoples “tend to be characterized not in any anthropologically specific terms, but as a lack or poorer form of the values of the centre.”
zh: 日本报界与殖民官僚机构至少产生了七份书面报告，记述以渡边大尉8月29日在大嵙崁驻军营地附近的试探性会面为起点、以角板山代表团9月12日返家为终点的种种事件。源自该使团的当时图像表明，1895年日本官员、作家与出版商并未把受民族学启发的多元主义范畴带到台湾。这些范畴是在殖民统治过程中就地形成并传播的。例如，桥口文藏与平野秋夫（Hirano Akio）大尉这样善于表述的官员，沿用了清代指称“野蛮”的术语（seiban，生番），并提到具体聚落及其首领的名字。然而，他们并未使用“泰雅”一词，也未把文化区附到岛上的族群地图之上。正如我们将看到的，日本在台湾生产的第一波原住民性图像，符合托马斯那种为前现代想象所构拟的理想型，其中其他民族“往往不是按各自具体的人类学特征来描述，而是被说成缺少中心社会的价值，或只以较差的方式体现了那些价值”。

en: The first published Japanese illustration of an Atayal person, based on an actual face-to-face encounter, appeared in an article in the September 29, 1895, issue of the mass-circulation

. The article included a crude sketch of the woman known as Papau Iron, later known as Habairon. This line drawing made no attempt to capture individual features but was rather a schematic drawing of facial tattoos. According to this article, Habairon was about thirty-five years old in 1895; she is described as a woman bearing forehead and cheek tattoos, which signified her betrothal (probably an incorrect interpretation). The other female in the party of six Atayal who trekked beyond Dakekan and traveled all the way to Taipei with Hashiguchi Bunzō and Governor Tanaka (see chapter 1) was described as a nineteen-year-old woman named Washa Buta (Washiiga in subsequent sources). Washiiga lacked tattoos because she had married a Chinese man at the age of sixteen. In contrast to the “savages” (

), Chinese did not require tattooing as part of the marriage contract, according to the report. The article also specified that female cheek tattoos consisted of four bands, indicated in the small line drawing referred to above. Despite its crudity, the newspaper drawing helped to fix the female Atayal face tattoo as one of the most easily recognizable icons of indigeneity in Taiwan.
zh: 日本首幅基于实际面对面接触而刊行的泰雅人图像，出现在广泛发行的《东京朝日新闻》（Tokyo Asahi shinbun）1895年9月29日号的一篇文章中。文章附有一幅粗陋的速写，画的是那位被称为帕保·伊隆（Papau Iron）、后来又称哈拜隆（Habairon）的女子。这幅线描并不试图捕捉个人特征，而是一幅纹面的示意图。据这篇文章，哈拜隆1895年时约三十五岁；她被描述为一个额头和面颊都有纹样的女子，这些纹身标志着她已订婚（很可能是错误的解读）。那支由六名泰雅人组成、跋涉离开大嵙崁并随桥口文藏与田中知事（见第1章）一路走到台北的队伍中，另一名女性被描述为十九岁、名叫瓦莎·布塔（Washa Buta，后续史料作Washiiga，即瓦希伊加）的女子。瓦希伊加没有纹身，因为她十六岁时嫁给了一个中国男人。据该报道，与“番人”（seiban，生番）不同，中国人并不把纹身作为婚约的一部分。文章还具体说明，女子纹在面颊上的图案由四道条纹组成，即上面提到的那幅小线描所标示的。尽管粗陋，这幅报纸线描却帮助把泰雅女性的纹面确立为台湾原住民性最易辨认的图像之一。

en: A second, more detailed sketch portrayed two participants in the Jiaobanshan encounter—an Atayal couple who did not travel all the way to Taipei—and appeared as the back-cover illustration for the 115th issue of the

children: Journal of the Tokyo Anthropological Society

en: (see

). This sketch illustrates a short narrative description of Japanese-Atayal diplomatic exchanges in September 1895. The narrative was penned by Hirano Akio, who accompanied the September 4, 1895, Hashiguchi mission to Caoling Ridge at the foot of Jiaobanshan. Like the

illustration, there is no attempt at ethnic or racial classification in the article. The personal names “Watan Nawi, Jiaobanshan village head, and Lemoi Maton, wife of Jiaobanshan village head” are attached, under the banner of
(savage attire). The illustration of Hirano’s note, like the cruder drawing in the

, focuses on facial tattoos as the marker of indigenous appearance, distinguishing between male and female patterns: men wore a vertical set of bars on their foreheads, while women wore the ear-to-mouth tattoos.

The clothing, ornaments, coiffure, and headdress of the Jiaobanshan residents are labeled with great care. The detached coiffures and ornaments abstracted isolated cultural elements from individual historical actors to put Taiwanese
within comparative ethnography’s global data set of cranial indexes, hair-strand widths, and ear shapes. At the same time, the faithfully rendered can and bottle in Lemoi Maton’s backsack (see

) situates the image in the shared time of frontier diplomacy, while the choice of headman Watan Nawi, who is a protagonist in the narrative account, elevates the illustration above the anonymity usually associated with “types.”
zh: 第二幅更详细的速写描绘了角板山接触中的两名参与者——一对并未一路走到台北的泰雅夫妇——并作为《东京人类学会杂志》第115期的封底插图刊出（见

）。这幅速写为一段关于1895年9月日本与泰雅外交交涉的简短叙事描述配图。该叙事由平野秋夫执笔，他曾随1895年9月4日桥口使团前往角板山脚下的草岭（Caoling Ridge）。与《东京朝日新闻》的插图一样，文章并未尝试作族群或种族分类。在“生番之服”（seiban no fuku）的标题下，附上了“角板山头目瓦坦·纳维（Watan Nawi），及角板山头目之妻莱莫伊·马顿（Lemoi Maton）”这两个名字。平野笔记的插图与《东京朝日新闻》那幅更粗陋的画一样，聚焦于作为原住民外貌标记的面部纹身，并区分男女纹样：男子额部纹有一组竖直条纹，女子则纹有从耳到口的纹身。
角板山居民的衣着、饰物、发式与头饰都被极其细致地标注。那些被单独拆离出来的发式与饰物，把孤立的文化元素从具体的历史行动者身上抽象出来，从而把台湾生番纳入比较民族学关于颅指数、发丝粗细与耳形的全球数据集。与此同时，莱莫伊·马顿背袋中那只被忠实描绘的罐子与瓶子（见
），使画中人物与当时参加边疆外交的各方处在同一个历史时刻；而选择叙事记述中的主角瓦坦·纳维头目，则使这幅插图超越了一般“类型”图像中人物不具名的做法。

. The next illustration, from the November 1895 issue of the general-audience magazine Fūzoku gahō, overlooked such niceties (see

en: According to the Fūzoku gahō article’s text (a faithful reproduction of excerpts from the official report filed by Hashiguchi Bunzō), the female indigenous interpreter Washiiga wears Chinese clothing and speaks an indigenous language, while the older woman, Habairon, was an unacculturated tattooed female in local garments. In the Fūzoku gahō illustration, however, the indigenous women lack tattoos altogether, and all of them wear a combination of Atayal capes and Chinese-style blouses.

In contrast to the ethnologically fastidious drawings in the anthropology bulletin described above, the men in the Fūzoku gahō wear facial tattoos that run from mouth to ear—a patently female pattern. More than any other detail, the tattoo mix-up confirms that the Fūzoku gahō artist was not working from photographs or eyewitness accounts. It is doubtful that the artist even read the text being illustrated.
zh: 据《风俗画报》文章的正文（忠实转载了桥口文藏所提交官方报告的摘录），原住民女通事瓦希伊加身穿中国服装、讲一种原住民语言，而年长的女子哈拜隆则是一个身着当地服饰、保留纹面、未习外来文化的女子。然而在《风俗画报》的插图中，原住民女子完全没有纹身，且全都穿着泰雅披肩与中式上衣的组合。
与上面描述的民族学简报中那种一丝不苟的图画相反，《风俗画报》中的男子面部纹身从口延伸到耳——分明是女性的纹样。比起任何其他细节，这一纹身错置更确证了《风俗画报》的画师并非依据照片或目击记述作画。甚至令人怀疑，画师是否读过他所配图的那段文字。

en: Nonetheless, one element of this otherwise fanciful image did have a referent. Kabayama Sukenori, Taiwan’s first governor-general, famously hosted the five Jiaobanshan emissaries and their interpreter Pu Chin in Taipei in September 1895 (see chapters 2 and 3). The inset portrait of Kabayama in
appears to be based on the commemorative photograph of the embassy.
zh: 尽管如此，这幅大多出于想象的画有一个细节确有根据。台湾首任总督桦山资纪于1895年9月在台北款待了五名角板山使者及其通译蒲靖（Pu Chin），此事广为人知（见第2、3章）。
中桦山的画中附绘的小肖像，似乎是以该使团的纪念照片为底本的。

en: In this version of the photograph (

), one Jiaobanshan emissary stares at the ground, while another is in a crouching position—not unlike the postures represented in the Fūzoku gahō illustration. The other Jiaobanshan emissaries adopt postures alien to the Fūzoku gahō drawing, however. These deviations from the photograph seem purposeful. The creative repositioning of Kabayama as a smartly attired military hero, who towers over the distorted figures of supplicant indigenes, in fact echoes 1874 wood-block prints of the Japanese expedition to Langqiao. As Robert Eskildsen has pointed out, colorful wood-block illustrations of the 1874 invasion in early Meiji-period newspapers were rife with exaggerated contrasts that posed heroic and upright Japanese soldiers lording it over gaudily attired and obsequious Paiwanese people.
By 1895, however, the smartly dressed Japanese military man (
and 37), with medals and uniform, formed a contrast to both the crouching indigenes and the pike-wielding samurai of the 1870s.
zh: 在这一版本的照片中（

），一名角板山使者盯着地面，另一名则呈蹲伏姿势——与《风俗画报》插图所表现的姿态不无相似。然而其他角板山使者采取的姿势却与《风俗画报》所画的姿态大不相同。这些对照片的偏离似乎是有意为之。画师重新安排人物位置，把桦山画成衣冠整饬的军队英雄，威严地俯视那些身形被改动、仿佛在哀求的原住民，实际上呼应了1874年日本征琅峤的木版画。正如罗伯特·埃斯基尔森（Robert Eskildsen）所指出的，明治早期报纸上关于1874年侵台的彩色木版插图充斥着夸张的对比：把英勇挺拔的日本士兵摆成居高临下之势，凌驾于衣着艳俗、卑躬屈膝的排湾人之上。
然而到1895年，那位衣着光鲜、佩勋章穿制服的日本军人（
、37），既与蹲伏的原住民形成对比，也与1870年代手持长矛的武士形成对比。

en: These portraits of the three emissaries Habairon, Motonaiban, and Washiiga were taken in Taipei or Dakekan walled city, to judge from the large masonry structure in the background. Whereas the Fūzoku gahō illustration attempted to establish a “savage territory” setting by replacing the built environment of the courtyard with a bamboo grove, Inō’s commissioned etching effaced the setting of the photograph completely by whiting out everything but the sitters. This form of decontextualization was a favorite tool of visual anthropologists in the Victorian era, because it facilitated global comparisons along certain narrowly defined somatic criteria. But unlike the decontextualized picture that illustrated Hirano Akio’s note (
), the illustration in
does not supply labels for items of material culture. Moreover, it is puzzling (in light of subsequent fabrications) that the facial tattoos described in the

article—the ethnographic marker of Atayal cultural distinction in this period—have been obscured, instead of accentuated, in this etching. Inō did, however, provide readers with a sharp illustration of Atayal textile wizardry, an element that was muted in Hirano’s otherwise more detailed sketch.
zh: 从背景中那座大型砖石建筑判断，哈拜隆、莫托奈班与瓦希伊加这三名使者的肖像，是在台北或大嵙崁城内拍摄的。《风俗画报》的插图试图用一片竹林取代庭院的建筑环境，以营造“蕃地”的场景；而伊能委托制作的蚀刻画则把除被摄者之外的一切全部涂白，彻底抹去了照片的环境。这种去情境化的手法是维多利亚时代视觉人类学家钟爱的工具，因为它便于沿某些界定狭窄的体质标准进行全球比较。但与为平野秋夫笔记配图的那幅去情境化图画（

en: The photograph in

was also staged during the Jiaobanshan embassy. It became a template for several mass-circulation images, including a photograph in a middle-school geography textbook. This portrait of Habairon, Washiiga, Marai, Ira Watan, and Motonaiban, with their interpreter Pu Chin, was shot in the governor-general’s reception hall in Taipei. As a comparison with

indicates, the Atayal guests sat in the governor-general’s and admiral’s wicker chairs for a smaller group portrait, in much less stiff poses. Ira Watan (seated) and Marai were brothers (aged twenty-one and eighteen, respectively), and Motonaiban was a forty-three-year-old widower (also seated). Washiiga and Pu Chin are standing on each side of Marai. Habairon is seated in a wicker chair. She appears to be playing a mouth harp, which also became, like facial tattoos, a marker for Atayal femininity in Japanese iconography.
zh: 的照片也是在角板山使团期间摆拍的。它成了若干广泛传播的图像的模板，包括一幅中学地理教科书中的照片。这幅哈拜隆、瓦希伊加、马来、伊拉·瓦坦与莫托奈班及其通译蒲靖的合影，摄于台北总督府的接待厅。与
对比可见，泰雅客人们坐在总督与海军大将的藤椅上，拍了一张人数更少的合影，姿势也不那么僵硬。伊拉·瓦坦（坐者）与马来是兄弟（分别为二十一岁和十八岁），莫托奈班则是个四十三岁的鳏夫（也坐着）。瓦希伊加与蒲靖分立马来两侧。哈拜隆坐在一张藤椅上。她似乎在吹奏口簧琴，而口簧琴也像面部纹身一样，成了日本图像志中泰雅女性的标记。

en: As we learned in chapter 1, newspaper and magazine accounts of the Jiaobanshan embassy attached personal names to all of the emissaries pictured in
, as well as the twenty-two people who greeted Hashiguchi outside Dakekan on September 8, 1895. This textbook illustration, however, is captioned
, with no other supporting information. The phrase translates to “native savages of Taiwan” and utilizes idiosyncratic characters. Japanese accounts published in Taiwan always use the character

, a carryover from the Qing period, to describe indigenes. In contrast, home-island publications used a mixed and inconsistent batch of signifiers for Taiwanese, even after standardized terminology had been fixed by the government. This 1898 textbook featured only this one photograph of Taiwanese people, making the Jiaobanshan emissaries representatives of the whole island for young readers.
zh: 正如我们在第1章所了解的，报纸与杂志关于角板山使团的记述，给

中所有使者都附上了人名，也给1895年9月8日在大嵙崁城外迎接桥口的二十二人附上了人名。然而这幅教科书插图仅题为“台湾土蛮”（Taiwan doban），没有附上其他说明。这个短语意为“台湾的土著番人”，用的是生僻奇特的汉字。在台湾刊行的日本方面的记述，总是用“蕃”（ban）字来描述原住民，这是清代的遗留。相比之下，日本内地的出版物对台湾人使用了一批混杂而不一致的指称符号，即便在政府已确定标准术语之后亦然。这部1898年的教科书只收录了这一张台湾人的照片，从而让角板山使者在年轻读者眼中成了全岛的代表。

en: The photograph in
reappeared in an early 1900s postcard, indicating its commercial appeal. The publishers used the more conventional term

to label the emissaries. Like other pre-geobody-era publications, this one lumps the Atayal men and women from the Jiaobanshan embassy together with a Puyuma man and a group of Bunun or Tsou men (sitters in the other two photos), under the blanket category “savage.”
zh: 的照片在20世纪初的一张明信片上重新出现，显示了它的商业吸引力。出版商用了更常规的术语“台湾生番”（Taiwan seiban）来标注这些使者。与其他地理体时代之前的出版物一样，这张明信片把角板山使团中的泰雅男女，与一名卑南男子及一群布农或邹族男子（另外两张照片中的被摄者）一起，笼统归入“蕃人”这一总括范畴。

en: The 1897, 1898, and 1900 editions of Sanseidō’s Teikoku chirigaku kyōkasho (Imperial geography textbook) present a radically altered version of the same photograph in a woodcut (see

). Here, the artist removed Habairon’s facial tattoos and mouth harp. The artist also depicted the seated Ira Watan as a standing model. The built environment, Pu Chin, Marai, Washiiga, and Motonaiban have been removed from the scene, probably to allow the reader a clearer view of the clothing and wicker chair that were thought to typify Taiwanese customs and manners (fūzoku) at the time. The caption, “a picture of Taiwanese” (
), obscures the indigenous or Atayal identity of the sitters. The Qing terms
(savage) and

(acculturated savage) for indigenes do appear in the text but not in connection with this illustration. The Sanseidō text equated eastern Taiwan with the “savage territory,” identifying it as home to the Mudan villagers who massacred Japanese victims back in 1874.
Because the tattoos on Habairon’s face are not apparent in the photograph that this etching has abstracted, it is not surprising that they were omitted. Compared to the Fūzoku gahō illustration in
, this textbook etching is a faithful representation of the photograph on which it is based.
zh: 三省堂《帝国地理学教科书》（Teikoku chirigaku kyōkasho）1897、1898与1900年版，以一幅木刻呈现了同一张照片被大幅改动的版本（见

）。在这里，画师去掉了哈拜隆的面部纹身与口簧琴，还把坐着的伊拉·瓦坦画成了站立的模特。建筑环境、蒲靖、马来、瓦希伊加与莫托奈班都被从画面中移除，大概是为了让读者更清楚地看到当时被认为能代表台湾风俗（fūzoku）的衣着与藤椅。图题“台湾人之图”（Taiwanjin no zu）掩盖了被摄者的原住民或泰雅身份。清代指称原住民的术语生番（seiban）与熟蕃（jukuban）确实出现在正文中，却与这幅插图无涉。三省堂的正文把台湾东部等同于“蕃地”，指认那里是1874年杀害日本受害者的牡丹社村民的家乡。
由于这幅画所据的照片上，哈拜隆面部的纹身并不明显，它们被略去也就不足为奇。与
的《风俗画报》插图相比，这幅教科书蚀刻画忠实再现了它所依据的照片。

en: Yet another iteration of the Jiaobanshan embassy photograph was published concurrently, in 1900 (see

). In this etching, the editors have retained Habairon’s original hand and arm positions but have removed her mouth harp. The male Ira Watan now wears female cheek-to-chin tattoos, while the male Marai has been endowed with ponytails. Sheep, banana trees, and buildings on stilts have replaced the courtyard of Kabayama’s reception area. Presumably, the point was to place the “savages” in their native habitat, symbolized here by elevated granaries, hilly topography, tropical foliage, and domesticated livestock. Although this was an educational text, it resembles the Fūzoku gahō illustration in its propensity for fabrication, enhancement, and misrepresentation.
