en: Late 1910 marked the end of large military maneuvers against Gaogan. By 1912 Jiaobanshan was sufficiently pacified to be considered the site for a visit from the Meiji emperor himself. For the emperor’s expected visit, a special reception hall, later depicted in numerous picture postcards, was erected in the main settlement area.

But, as a privately produced 1915 travel guide reminded its readers, even though the area was undergoing reclamation and the population was increasing, the next stop, Gaogan, was still garrisoned for defense against indigenes.
zh: 1910年末标志着针对高干的大规模军事行动的结束。到1912年，角板山已在相当程度上被日方控制，当局甚至考虑安排明治天皇亲临。为天皇预期的到访，主要聚落区建起了一座专门的接待厅，后来出现在无数图画明信片上。
但是，正如一本民间制作的1915年旅行指南提醒读者的，尽管该地区正在垦殖、人口正在增长，下一站高干却仍驻军以防原住民。

en: Just after this 1915 guide appeared, Jiaobanshan became an obligatory stop on imperial inspection tours of Taiwan. The Imperial Household Ministry archive in Tokyo contains several lavishly illustrated albums of these tours, which included those of Prince Kan’in in 1916, Crown Prince Hirohito in 1923, and Prince Chichibu in 1925. During this liminal decade, the Japanese royals affixed commercial photographs and their own snapshots to keepsake albums. The overall impression is of Jiaobanshan as a borderland that was fast becoming an indigenous theme park.
zh: 就在这本1915年指南问世后不久，角板山成了皇室巡视台湾时必停的一站。东京的宫内省档案藏有数册这些巡访的精美写真帖，其中包括1916年闲院宫、1923年裕仁皇太子与1925年秩父宫的巡访。在这个过渡性的十年里，日本皇室成员把商业照片与他们自己的快照贴进纪念册。整体印象是，角板山是一片正迅速变成原住民主题公园的边地。

en: By 1920, the light-gauge pushcart railway that connected the town of Jiaobanshan to the railway stop at Daxi (the new name for Dakekan) had become a conduit for tourists, freight, and officials. Travelers ascended the mountain pushed by two Taiwanese laborers, with rest stations and inns all along the way.
A 1921 travel guide emphasized the scenery and the pushcart ride. It also created the boilerplate for subsequent Jiaobanshan descriptions in the official travel guides:
zh: 到1920年，那条把角板山街与大溪（大嵙崁的新名）火车站连接起来的轻便台车铁路，已成了游客、货物与官员的通道。旅客由两名台湾劳工推着台车上山，沿途一路都有休息站与客栈。
一本1921年的旅行指南强调了风景与台车乘坐体验。它还为后续官方旅行指南中的角板山描述创造了样板文字：

en: Nine
and seven

southeast of Daxi [Dakekan] walled city is the savage border. If you clamber your way up, you’ll be able to intimately inspect conditions among the aborigines. This area is zigzagged and steep. Climbing up the mountain path by tramway is extremely slow, but descending is extremely fast, for a speedy return. At the top of the mountain, things suddenly open up into orderly quadrilateral residences; this is Jiaobanshan. There is the balmy fragrance of camphor and the reception hall built from building materials from Arisan. This area is a tableland that commands a view upstream of the Dakekan ravine and is ringed by verdant linked ridgelines.... It is thus known not only for its steep terrain but also for its spectacular scenery.
zh: 大溪〔大嵙崁〕城东南九里七町，便是生番界。若你攀援而上，就能近距离察看蕃人状况。这一带曲折而陡峭。乘台车沿山径上行极慢，下行却极快，便于速返。到了山顶，眼前豁然开朗，出现整齐的方整的住宅；这就是角板山。这里有樟脑的清香，还有用阿里山建材建成的接待厅。这一带是一片台地，向上游可以俯瞰大嵙崁溪谷，四周环绕着苍翠相连的山脊线……它因此不仅以地势陡峭闻名，也以风景壮丽著称。

en: Sōyama Takeshi writes that “indigenous territory” tourism had become a mainstay by 1924, when the “injuries from indigene violence” had finally subsided and railways extended to the interior.

The 1924 version of the railway guide boasted that Jiaobanshan was not only a “strategic hold in aborigine administration” but also the site of two Japanese inns, a police station dispatch office, a post office, a school for aborigine children (
), an aborigine trading post (

), a Mitsui Corporation outpost, and a camphor company collection depot. The guide also mentioned that visitors could pick up valuable indigenous manufactures at good prices. Jiaobanshan, concluded this entry, could not be overlooked as a place to “get to know the aborigines.”
zh: 曾山武（Sōyama Takeshi）写道，到1924年，“蕃地”旅游已成为一项支柱，那时所谓“蕃害”终于平息，铁路也延伸进了内陆。
1924年版的铁路指南夸耀说，角板山不仅是“理蕃的战略要冲”，还是两家日式旅馆、一个警察派出所、一家邮局、一所蕃人儿童学校（
）、一个蕃人贸易站（
）、一处三井会社办事处，以及一家樟脑公司收购站的所在地。指南还提到，游客能以好价钱买到珍贵的原住民制品。该条目总结道，角板山作为一个“认识蕃人”的地方，不容忽视。

en: Jiaobanshan’s reputation even extended to the rare foreign visitor. In 1925, H. L. Bagallay of the British Foreign Office described Jiaobanshan as “a ‘show village’ about twenty-five miles from the capital, where ‘tame’ savages are exhibited to official visitors and tourists...”
The 1927, 1930, and 1934 Taiwan Railway guides repeated the 1924 description above, suggesting that ethnic tourism had become routinized in Jiaobanshan by the early 1930s.
zh: 角板山的连少数到访的外国人也知道角板山。1925年，英国外交部的巴加利（H. L. Bagallay）把角板山描述为“一座距首府约二十五英里的‘展示村’，向官方访客与游客展示‘驯服的’生番……”
1927、1930与1934年的《台湾铁路指南》重复了上述1924年的描述，表明到1930年代初，角板山的族群旅游已成了常规项目。

en: The 1934 guide adds that Jiaobanshan, Wulai (see above), and Alishan, all sites for indigenous tourism, were now in “normally administered territory.” However, the official 1935 Indigenous Household Register statistics indicate that all Atayal and Tsou peoples—the indigenous peoples of these three sites—resided beyond administered territory. Therefore, tourists were actually chatting with and photographing indigenes who were either visiting the tourist sites as employees or who had removed to the normally administered territory.

In these three popular sites, tourists could have the best of both worlds. They could enter Jiaobanshan, Wulai, or Alishan without filling out burdensome paperwork and paying extra fees required to travel beyond the line between special and normal administration and “experience savage life” without unduly upsetting their tour itineraries.

Ease of access and proximity to civilization were indeed the major themes in touristic imagery of Jiaobanshan in the 1930s. Photos of Japanese schools (run by police officers) filled with indigenous children and Hinomaru flags decorated magazines, atlases, and picture postcards of the 1920s and 1930s (
). Much of the textual rhetoric accompanying these images extolled the conversion of a former head-hunting people into rice-growing, peace-loving subjects of the emperor.
zh: 1934年的指南补充说，角板山、乌来（见上文）与阿里山这些原住民旅游地点，如今都位于“普通行政区”内。然而，官方1935年的原住民户口登记统计表明，所有泰雅与邹人——这三处的原住民——都居住在普通行政区以外。因此，游客实际与之聊天、为之拍照的原住民，要么是作为雇员到访这些旅游地点，要么是已迁居到普通行政区。
在这三个热门地点，游客可以两全其美。他们无需填写繁琐文书，也不用缴纳跨入特别行政区所需的额外费用，就能进入角板山、乌来或阿里山，“体验生番生活”，又不至于过度打乱自己的行程。
易于抵达与临近文明，确实是1930年代角板山旅游图像的主题。由日本警察经办的学校里坐满原住民儿童、挂着日之丸旗，这样的照片点缀着1920与1930年代的杂志、地图集与图画明信片（
）。伴随这些图像的文字言辞，大多颂扬把一个昔日的猎首民族转化为种稻、爱好和平的天皇臣民。

en: Recall that in 1895, culturally hybrid figures—the Atayal woman Washiiga in a Chinese blouse or the Atayal man Pu Chin wearing a queue—were prominent in Japanese imagery because interpreters were the point of access to Jiaobanshan. Anthropologist Inō Kanori, in 1896, abstracted a photograph of Jiaobanshan residents taken in built environments by whiting out its background to produce more suitably anthropological types. Into the 1910s and even the 1920s, Chinese blouses like Washiiga’s were prominent in photographs of Atayal women in borderland junctions such as Jiaobanshan or Wulai, as exemplified by Mori Ushinosuke’s photo of a “Dakekan tribe woman” in July 1906, at the height of the camphor wars near Jiaobanshan, and by dozens of picture postcards.

By the 1930s, however, Chinese blouses were scarce in Japanese photography, while Japanese garments became commonplace. For ethnic-tourism operators, the question became how to balance the messages of progress and exoticism by packaging accessible villagers as avatars of a more primitive and even timeless past.
zh: 回想1895年，身兼两种文化特征的人物——穿汉式上衣的泰雅女子瓦希伊加，或留辫子的泰雅男子蒲靖——在日本图像中十分醒目，因为日方要与角板山的居民接触，须借助这些通事。人类学家伊能嘉矩1896年涂白一张在房屋之间拍摄的角板山居民照片的背景，抽去具体现场，以绘出更符合人类学范式的人物类型。直到1910年代乃至1920年代，像瓦希伊加那样的汉式上衣，在角板山或乌来这类边地交汇点的泰雅女子照片中仍很醒目，森丑之助1906年7月——正值角板山附近樟脑战争最高潮——拍摄的一名“大嵙崁族女子”照片，以及数十张图画明信片，便是例证。
然而到1930年代，汉式上衣在日本摄影中已稀少，日式服装则变得寻常。对族群旅游经营者而言，问题变成了：如何把游客眼前就能见到的村民包装成所谓更原始、甚至不随时间改变的过去的化身，从而平衡进步与异国情调这两种讯息。

en: One answer was found in the skillful use of graphic arts to construct Jiaobanshan as a gateway into the Atayal geobody. This effect was achieved by manipulating particular icons of Atayal ethnicity such as facial tattoos, tobacco pipes, back-strap looms, and wicker backpacks. These icons of the unique Atayal cultural repertoire were detached from lived environments, bundled together, and marketed as portable keepsakes from an unspoiled corner of the savage territory. ), this woman was rendered into line art and then imaginatively placed in a new setting. But instead of the background that corresponded to blank space on the 1905 census map (

and 39), the Wakayama Prefecture–based Taishō Company placed her in front of a mountain range and Jiaobanshan’s trademark suspension bridge. Tourists walked single file along this popular attraction, which connected the souvenir stands and the model school for indigenes to the mountains. The sitter in

was photographed in front of a fence and a neatly edged footpath on level ground, presumably in Jiaobanshan’s model ethnic village. The graphic artist thereafter transformed her into a highlander guarding a secret passageway for the postcard sleeve titled Bankai no hikyō (Undiscovered savage border).

中的被摄者，是在平地上一道围栏与一条边缘整齐的小径前被拍照的，大概是在角板山的示范性的原住民观光村。平面艺术家随后把她转化为一名守卫秘密通道的高山住民，用于题为《蕃界之秘境》（Bankai no hikyō）的明信片封套。

en: Advances in reprographic technology allowed for further abstractions and mash-ups. This sitter’s tattooed face, as well as her backpack, were logoized into monochrome stamps that adorned other cards in the set, tying otherwise placid scenes that connoted settled life and domesticity to the tattooed mascot who greeted visitors to the mountainous and supposedly mysterious savage territory (
). The photographs on the cards themselves depict an enclosed, flat settlement composed of Japanese-constructed dwellings and public buildings. But the last card in the set (

) depicts the setting, much like the sleeve, as an extension of Taiwan’s central cordillera, rather than as the island’s most convenient place to sample indigenous culture in the course of a weekend tour.
zh: 复制技术的进步允许进一步抽取并重组图像元素。这名被摄者的纹面，以及她的背篓，被制成单色图记，装饰着套组中的其他明信片，把那些原本平静、暗示定居生活与家居的场景，系于那位纹面吉祥物——她迎接着来到这片多山、据称神秘的生番领土的访客（
）。明信片上的照片本身描绘的是一个封闭、平坦的聚落，由由日方兴建的住屋和公共建筑组成。但套组中最后一张（
）却像封套一样，把这一场景描绘为台湾中央山脉的延伸，而非该岛在周末游程中最便于体验原住民文化的地方。

en: Jiaobanshan worked as a show village, then, because it could provide the experience of “savage Taiwan” in such a way as to suggest that this “tame” settlement was indeed an exemplar of the rest of aborigine country. In this example, the deft use of imaginative geography, cropping, extrapolation, and logoization created a snapshot of Atayalness that was quickly apprehended and could be brought back or sent to Taipei, Gaoxiong, Tokyo, or Osaka in the form of a souvenir postcard set.
zh: 因此，角板山之所以能充当“展示村”，是因为它能以这样一种方式提供“生番台湾”的体验：暗示这个“驯服的”聚落确实是其他蕃地的缩影。在这个例子中，对想象地理、裁切、外推与标志化的巧妙运用，创造了一个让人一眼就能认出的泰雅族形象，并能以纪念明信片套组的形式被带回或寄往台北、高雄、东京或大阪。

en: In 1935 the government-general hosted the Taiwan Hakurankai (Taiwan Expo) to celebrate its fortieth anniversary. One Taiwan Expo album held dozens of photographs that also appeared in the monthly bulletin

(Aborigine policemen’s companion), published by the Keimukyoku Ribanka (Police Bureau, Aborigine Affairs Section) and in numerous postcard designs. These photographs were mostly shot by Segawa Kōkichi, an intimate of the Aborigine Affairs section chief Suzuki Hideo, and successor to Mori Ushinosuke as Japan’s official portrait photographer of anthropological types.

In the Atayal section of the album, the Jiaobanshan photo shows the “Japanizing” of Atayal models in “various kinds of antiquated and new-style clothing.” Right below it is a photo of Atayal from the Wushe settlement of Paalan, the home of Iwan Roba0, Kondō the Barbarian’s first wife. en: To suture these two photos together ideologically—the one displaying Japanization and the other what is being Japanized—the first page of the
section of the souvenir book subsumes both images under the second-order geobody Atayal (

). Because it was located in Atayal country and was configured horizontally within a common two-dimensional geobody, along with the visibly unassimilated inhabitants of Paalan, Jiaobanshan could represent the whole of untouched northern Taiwan, while exhibiting imperial progress toward Japanizing a wilderness that, a mere thirty years earlier, could only be represented as a borderland on the extremity of the Qing Empire. Here, in the dioramas, photographs, and ethnic maps of the 1935 exhibition, we find the fruition of the tandem operations of cartographic and racialist geobody construction. Whether strolling the fairgrounds, making a day trip to Wulai or Jiaobanshan to buy souvenirs, or perusing scholarly, commercial, or official photography of Taiwan Indigenous Peoples, Japanese people could quickly apprehend 1930s Atayal culture and extrapolate it across the surface of Taiwan’s interior. The ensemble of artifacts, maps, performances, images, and texts associated with Jiaobanshan represented Taiwan’s aborigines at once as a population frozen in time and as a race that had been rescued from the neglect of the Qing dynasty by energetic Japanese officials.
zh: 要在意识形态上把这两张照片缝合在一起——一张展示日本化，另一张展示正在被日本化的对象——纪念册泰雅部分的第一页把两幅图像都归入二阶地理体“泰雅”之下（

）。由于角板山位于泰雅地域，并与芭兰那些明显未被同化的居民一起，在地图上被并列纳入同一个二维地理体，它便能代表整个未受触动的北台湾，同时展示日本帝国使一片荒野日本化的进展——而仅仅三十年前，这片荒野还只能被表征为清帝国极边缘的一处边地。在这里，在1935年展览的立体布景、照片与族群地图中，我们看到了以制图和种族分类共同建构地理体的成果。无论是在博览会场漫步、到乌来或角板山一日游购买纪念品，还是浏览学术的、商业的或官方的台湾原住民摄影，日本人都能迅速领会1930年代的泰雅文化，并推想台湾整个内陆都是如此。与角板山相关联的器物、地图、表演、图像与文本的整体，把台湾原住民既表征为一个冻结于时间中的人口，又表征为一个被精力充沛的日本官员从清朝的忽视中拯救出来的种族。

en: For those who could not make the trip to an exhibition or a souvenir stand, government-published textbooks—compulsory reading for nearly the whole of Japan—employed the same stratagems. When the Ministry of Education finally revised its elementary-school geography texts in 1910 and 1919, it partially heeded Inō Kanori’s criticisms by including portraits of Han Taiwanese. Each edition also updated its indigenous imagery, both relying on Mori’s photographs from Wulai and Rimogan. The 1910 edition displayed profile mugshot etchings of Pazzeh of Wulai and Marai of Rimogan and captioned each as generic
(savages). The 1919 edition substituted Yūgai of Rimogan for Pazzeh of Wulai to present readers with a male and a female icon from the same settlement. Mori’s June 1903 photograph (see
) was the source of this illustration.
zh: 对于那些无法前往展览会或纪念品摊的人，政府出版的教科书——几乎是全日本的强制读物——采用了同样的策略。当文部省终于在1910与1919年修订其小学地理教科书时，它部分采纳了伊能嘉矩的批评，收入了台湾汉人的肖像。每一版也更新了其原住民图像，都依赖森在乌来与利莫干拍摄的照片。1910年版展示了乌来的帕泽赫与利莫干的马来的档案照式的侧面版画，并把每张都图注为泛称的“蕃人”（banjin，即生番）。1919年版用利莫干的尤盖取代乌来的帕泽赫，向读者呈现来自同一聚落的一男一女两幅代表性人像。森1903年6月的照片（见

en: A couple of months before Mori photographed the Rimogan couple, he also took a scenic photograph of Atayal dwellings near Wulai (

). This composition was reproduced in several government and commercial publications throughout the colonial period. The updated 1919 textbook rendered these photographs from distinct Atayal settlements into emblems of the same savage territory by inserting the Rimogan portrait of Yūgai and Marai into a Wulai setting (see

). For the editors of the 1903, 1910, and 1919 geography textbooks, then, all indigenous people constituted a subpopulation. The 1919 version that merged Wulai and Rimogan imagery added a physical setting to cement the view that indigenes, no matter where they were photographed, were essentially hill people.

en: INDIGENOUS MODERNITY: A TWO-PART INVENTION
zh: 原住民现代性：二部创意曲

en: A careful student of Taiwanese history and Japanese colonial rhetoric, upon attending the 1935 Taiwan Expo, might have asked why, after forty years of colonial rule, the indigenous people of Paalan (

) were still dressing in handwoven fabrics, living in drafty slate houses, and working in pursuits far removed from the booming capitalist economy of the lowlands. After all, the Japanese state had managed to mobilize resources sufficient to win the Russo-Japanese War (1904–05), dislodge the Germans from Shandong in 1915, and overrun the three northeastern provinces of China in 1931. Why had it made such a poor showing in the uplands of Taiwan after four decades of opportunity?
zh: 一位细察台湾史和日本殖民话语的研究者，在参观1935年台湾博览会时，或许会问：为何经过四十年殖民统治，芭兰的原住民（
）仍穿着手织布料、住在透风的石板屋里、从事着与低地蓬勃资本主义经济相去甚远的营生？毕竟，日本国家曾成功动员足够资源，赢得日俄战争（1904–05）、1915年把德国人逐出山东、1931年侵占中国东北三省。为何已有四十年经营之机，它在台湾山地却表现如此之差？
body.review: 原书此处写1915年。德军1914年在青岛战败，1915年的中日交涉涉及德国在山东的权益。芭兰人物照片见图57下图。

en: The answer to this question brings us back to Foucault’s formulation of the “disciplinary society.” A number of scholars of Japanese colonial rule in Taiwan have observed that, in the lowlands where some 97 percent of Taiwanese lived, the Japanese colonial state was able to scale back its raw displays of punitive power by 1915 or so, with the crushing of the Ta-pa-ni rebellion.
At the same time, the extension of the

system and the development of commercial law, public health and education, commoditization labor, and a system of safeguards for the protection of private property made great inroads into the warp and woof of daily life, in cities and in the countryside. This interlocking set of institutions and practices created a Taiwanese political economy that paid more to Tokyo in tax revenue than it cost to maintain in terms of expenditures taken from the national operating budget in Tokyo. A critical mass of lowland Han Taiwanese were, however grudgingly, bought into a disciplinary order. The incentive system that garnered this buy-in was itself expensive. To provide title deeds to land, access to commercial courts, irrigation projects, harbors, schools, hospitals, and other improvements, in such a way that they are in fact paid for by the colonized people themselves, required a “big bang” on the order of Gotō Shinpei’s large spending spree of the early twentieth century. By the mid-1910s, the state—in varied degrees of alliance with Taiwanese capitalists, smallholders, professionals, policemen, officials, and

heads—had created a population that could not only produce surplus wealth but would also surrender enough of it to the government to pay for its own regulation. This form of society, wherein population increases redound to the power of the state (instead of to its detriment), is the desideratum of the disciplinary state.
zh: 这个问题的答案把我们带回福柯对“规训社会”的表述。若干研究日本在台殖民统治的学者观察到，在约97%台湾人居住的低地，日本殖民国家到1915年前后、随着噍吧哖（Ta-pa-ni）起义被镇压，已能缩减其公然展示惩罚权力的做法。

与此同时，保甲制度的延伸，以及商法、公共卫生与教育、劳动的商品化，还有一套保护私有财产的保障体系的发展，深刻改变了城市和乡村的日常生活。这一套相互扣合的制度与实践，使台湾形成了这样一种政治经济：东京获得的台湾税收，高于日本国库划拨的台湾行政开支。已有足够多的低地台湾汉人在激励之下接受了规训秩序，尽管并不情愿。赢得这种认同的激励体系本身代价高昂。要以实际上由被殖民者自己买单的方式，提供地契、商事法庭的准入、灌溉工程、港口、学校、医院及其他改良，需要一次集中投入，规模相当于后藤新平在二十世纪初的大笔支出。到1910年代中期，国家——在与台湾资本家、小农户、专业人士、警察、官员与保甲头人不同程度的结盟中——已造就了一个不仅能生产剩余财富、而且愿意向政府交出足够份额以支付自身规训费用的人口。这种社会形态，其中人口增长增益国家权力（而非损害它），正是规训国家的理想目标。

en: Yao Jen-to has concurred, asserting that the Japanese created a disciplinary society and biopolitical regime in Taiwan based on his interpretation of the state’s profligate use of statistics and its vaunted interest in “forcing Taiwanese to be healthy.” Curiously, Yao overlooks the fact that the first Japanese census left the indigenous territories completely blank and that much of Taiwan still fell outside the Government-General’s tax base when Japan surrendered in 1945.
zh: 姚人多对此表示赞同，他基于自己对国家大规模运用统计，并标榜自己在“迫使台湾人保持健康”的解读，断言日本人在台湾创造了一个规训社会与生命政治体制。奇怪的是，姚忽略了一个事实：日本首次人口普查把原住民领土完全留白，而且到1945年日本投降时，台湾很大一部分仍落在总督府税基之外。

en: The lands beyond the pale of Yao’s analysis were at first defined as a zone of special administration, or the indigenous territories, because they were little known to Japanese administrators and did not appear on the ready-made grid inherited from the Qing. To rectify this situation, Sakuma Samata initiated his own “big bang” in the form of coordinated military offensives that culminated in the gokanen keikaku riban jigyō (five-year plan to control the aborigines). As we have seen, this scorched-earth approach succeeded to the extent that rebelling subjects were mostly disarmed. The mountain territories were, in fact, made safe for land and forest surveys. Abutting forests were cleared of toll states, and the obfuscating layer of
(bicultural interpreters) that complicated relationships between primary producers and camphor capitalists was expelled from the savage border.
zh: 姚分析范围之外的土地，起初被界定为一个特别行政地带，即原住民领土，因为日本行政官员对它们知之甚少，它们也并未被纳入承袭自清代、已有明确划分的行政体系。为纠正这一状况，佐久间左马太以协同军事攻势的形式发动了他自己的“大爆炸”，最后发展为“五年理蕃计划”（gokanen keikaku riban jigyō）。如我们所见，这套焦土策略在一定程度上奏效，大部分反抗者被缴械。山地领土事实上变得可供土地与森林调查安全作业。邻近林地的收费政体被扫除，而处于初级生产者与樟脑资本家之间、使双方关系复杂而难以看清的通事（tongshi，即通晓两种文化的译员）这一中介群体，则被逐出生番界。

en: This is all to say that the post-Sakuma “aborigine district” was not a product of state neglect. After 1910 especially, and into the 1930s, the state proceeded to inventory, catalog, regulate, regiment, spatially array, and even nurture indigenous populations in order to extract wealth from the highlands. While this panoptical and surveillance-like activity bore superficial marks of discipline, it excluded the most important element: the state did not produce individuals in Taiwan’s indigenous territories. Rather, it produced tribes, settlements, ethnic groups, and aborigines. Collective punishment, ad hoc justice, forced relocation, fixed prices at trading posts, poorly compensated corvée labor, and nonrecognition of ownership rights in forest lands were the lot of those who lived under special administration in colonial Taiwan. In these lands beyond the pale of the Han-dominated lowlands, the state did not invest in banks, courts, high schools, train stations, and other discipline-inducing infrastructure. In the specially administered areas, Taiwanese could not secure title deeds, compete for status in a public school system, open businesses in bustling port towns, or sell agricultural produce, hunted goods, or handicrafts at market prices.
zh: 这一切是说，后佐久间时代的“蕃地”并非国家忽视的产物。尤其在1910年之后、直到1930年代，国家着手调查、登记、管制、编组、重新安排原住民的居住空间，甚至投入资源照料他们，以便从高地榨取财富。虽然这种全景敞视式的监控带有与规训有表面上的相似，它却排除了最重要的要素：国家在台湾原住民领土并不生产个体。相反，它生产部落、聚落、族群与蕃人。集体惩罚、临事而定的司法裁决、强制迁居、贸易站的固定价格、报酬低微的徭役劳动，以及对林地所有权的不承认，正是殖民台湾生活在特别行政之下者的命运。在这些汉人主导低地范围之外的土地上，国家不投资于银行、法庭、中学、火车站及其他诱发规训的基础设施。在特别行政区域，台湾人无法取得地契、无法在公立学校体系中争取个人进身的机会、无法在繁忙港口城镇开店，也无法按市场价格出售农产品、猎获物或手工艺品。

en: Given the bounty of natural resources to be found in the highlands and the alacrity with which indigenes learned the Japanese language and new trades, it might seem puzzling that the state did not press its apparent advantage in 1915 to bring the highlands within the profitable zone of disciplinary society. The lower Hengchun Paiwan peoples, led by Pan Bunkiet and then his son, provide a telling example. These villages were of mixed Han,

, and Paiwan residence. They were included in the regularly administered territory of Taiwan during the period Matsuoka Tadasu has characterized as one of temporary expediency. By 1906 almost all of the lower Hengchun Paiwan settlements were recognized as being sufficiently settled to pay taxes. Therefore, their territories would no longer be closed to immigrants, and they would fall under a structure of surveillance similar to neighboring

units. Thus, along with the Amis and the Puyuma of the eastern rift valley, the lower Hengchun Paiwan were, in many respects, integrated into the empire. Nonetheless, as culture bearers and denizens of ethnically defined subgeobodies, they occupied a liminal space: they were legally, economically, and administratively considered “civilized,” but they were still accounted for in population counts as members of non-Han ethnic groups—as Paiwans.

Moreover, they were still represented at tourist sites, in exhibitions, and in media as colorful examples of Taiwan’s ethnic diversity. In a word, there was more to the permanent bifurcation of Taiwan into ethnically demarcated zones of difference than uneven capitalist development or relative levels of state neglect and oppression.
zh: 鉴于高地自然资源之丰饶，以及原住民学习日语与新营生之敏捷，国家未在1915年趁其明显优势把高地纳入规训社会的有利可图地带，似乎令人费解。下恒春的排湾人，先由潘文杰、后由其子领导，提供了一个说明问题的例子。这些村落是汉人、熟蕃与排湾人混居的。在松冈达所刻画为权宜之计的那段时期，它们被纳入台湾的普通行政区。到1906年，几乎下恒春所有排湾聚落都被认为已定居程度已足以纳税。因此，它们的领土不再对移民封闭，并将落入一套与邻近保甲单位类似的监视结构。于是，连同东部纵谷的阿美与卑南，下恒春排湾人在许多方面被整合进了帝国。尽管如此，作为文化承载者与按族群界定的次级地理体的居民，他们处在不同类别之间：他们在法律、经济与行政上被视为“文明”，但在人口统计中仍被算作非汉族群成员——算作排湾人。
此外，他们在旅游地点、展览会与媒体中，仍被表征为台湾族群多样性的多彩范例。一言以蔽之，台湾被永久二分为族群划界的差异地带，其中缘由不止于资本主义发展的不平衡，或国家忽视与压迫的相对程度。

en: There are two major reasons for the arrested development of disciplinary society in colonial Taiwan. The first is negative. When TGG visionaries first mapped out schemes for ruling the island, Taiwan was Japan’s only colony. As Japan added colonies (Karafuto and the Kwantung leased territory in 1905, Korea in 1910), the relative size and importance of Taiwan’s uplands in the grand scheme of things shrank. Consequently, the cost of building a capitalist infrastructure that could produce a self-regulating disciplinary society in upland Taiwan was beyond the reach of the government-general by 1915. As we saw in chapters 1 and 2, even when the empire was relatively flush after the Sino-Japanese War, savage-border policy was run on the cheap. Although Sakuma’s five-year plan to control the aborigines was announced with great fanfare and a ¥15 million budget, the funds dried up before the work was finished, and Japan declared victory in 1914 out of exhaustion.
zh: 殖民台湾规训社会发展受阻，有两大原因。第一项是财力不足。当总督府的政策规划者最初规划统治该岛的方案时，台湾是日本唯一的殖民地。随着日本增添殖民地——1905年的桦太（库页岛南部）与关东租借地、1910年的朝鲜——台湾山地在整个大局中的相对规模与重要性缩小了。因此，到1915年，建造一套能在台湾山地产生自我规训社会的资本主义基础设施的成本，已超出总督府的能力所及。如我们在第1、2章所见，即便甲午战争后帝国相对充裕，生番界政策也是省钱办事。尽管佐久间的五年计划理蕃事业以大张旗鼓与1500万日元预算宣布，资金却在工作完成前枯竭，日方因资源消耗殆尽，于1914年宣布胜利。

en: Nonetheless, from 1915 through 1925, a series of land and population surveys was conducted throughout the highlands. These projects set the stage for not only large forest giveaways but also forced migration movements and programs to transition indigenes into intensive agriculture. As Matsuoka Tadasu has argued, up until 1915, special administration was a temporary expedient—the original plan was to economically integrate the island economy.

But despite the intrusions of irrigation projects, village relocation, and police government, the TGG policies kept the indigenous peoples intact as a separate population. Labor migration to the plains was discouraged; the fruits of intensive agriculture were not exported beyond the highlands but were consumed in the highlands themselves; and a majority of indigenes never paid taxes. Forced migration only occurred

the aborigine territory: peoples were not moved to areas under regular administration. Matsuoka documents a number of positions, including that of Governor-General Den Kenjirō, that argued for the dissolution of the indigenous territory and Taiwan’s administrative integration. Nonetheless, the government-general halted in its tracks at the old savage border, partly out of bureaucratic inertia but also because the Wushe uprising showed that indigenes were in need of different treatment. Moreover, argues Matsuoka, Japanese scholar-officials in the post-Wushe era tipped the balance in favor of preservationist policies.
zh: 尽管如此，从1915到1925年，当局在各处山地调查土地与人口，为大批林地的无偿划拨、强制迁移以及推进原住民转入集约农业铺平道路。正如松冈达所论，直到1915年，特别行政都是一种权宜之计——原计划是把全岛纳入同一个经济体系。

但尽管有灌溉工程、村落迁居与警察治理的侵入，总督府政策仍使原住民作为一个人口群体继续与其他人口分开。向平原的劳动迁移受到劝阻；集约农业的成果不销往山地以外，而在高地自身消费；大多数原住民从不纳税。强制迁移只发生在蕃人领土内部：各民族不被迁往普通行政区域。松冈记录了若干主张，包括田健治郎总督的主张，论证解散原住民领土、实现台湾行政一体化。尽管如此，总督府却在旧生番界骤然止步，部分出于官僚惰性，但也因为雾社起义表明原住民需要不同对待。此外，松冈论证道，雾社事件后的日本学者型官员把天平拨向了保存主义政策。

en: Matsuda Kyōko’s analysis of Japanese policies, practices, and representational strategies in 1930s Taiwan confirms Matsuoka’s hypothesis from a different vantage. Most importantly, Matsuda demonstrates that preservationism reached beyond the small circle of intellectuals discussed above and was translated into actual policy. This brand of preservationism, Matsuda argues, forced policemen, exhibition organizers, tourism operators, and administrators to walk a fine line. On the one hand, they needed to demonstrate the efficacy of Japanization programs and policies aimed at turning supposedly rootless, violent, wandering hunters into settled and peaceful agriculturalists. On the other hand, these same social engineers recoiled in horror at the prospect of indigenes becoming dandies who might participate in the consumer culture and urban cosmopolitanism that characterized Taipei in the 1930s. The reformed yet not modern indigenous Taiwanese would always be toilers on the soil, possessed of beautiful customs. They were an ethnically separate population requiring the ministrations of a trained corps of Japanese aborigine policemen-administrators to both ease them away from the worst of their old customs and shield them from the worst excesses of modernity.
zh: 松田京子（Matsuda Kyōko）对1930年代日本在台湾的政策、实践与表征策略的分析，从另一视角印证了松冈的假说。最重要的是，松田表明保存主义超出了上文讨论的那个小知识分子圈子，并被转化为实际政策。松田论证道，这种保存主义，迫使警察、展览组织者、旅游经营者与行政官员小心拿捏分寸。一方面，他们需要展示日本化计划与政策的成效——这些计划旨在把据称无根、暴力、游荡的猎人变成定居而和平的农耕者。另一方面，同样是这些致力于改造社会的人，却对原住民变成花花公子、可能参与1930年代台北那种消费文化与都市世界主义的前景，惊恐退缩。按这种设想，台湾原住民虽经改造，仍不会成为现代人，将永远是土地上的劳作者，拥有美好的习俗。他们是一个族群上分离的人口，需要一支训练有素的日本理蕃警察兼行政者队伍来照料，既引导他们脱离旧习俗中最恶劣的部分，又使他们免遭现代化最恶劣的一面冲击。

en: The evidence for Matsuda’s general claim is abundant. For one, whereas indigenous sightseeing programs in the late 1890s through the 1910s brought small numbers of headmen and traditional leaders to urban Japan to scare them into submission by displaying Japanese military equipment and the advanced infrastructure of the home islands, tours in the 1930s involved large groups drawn from aborigine youth corps to demonstration farms within indigenous territory or to other flourishing agricultural sites in Taiwan or Japan. The goal was no longer to implant visions of Japan’s overwhelming modernity and power but to educate indigenous people practically for crop production and stock breeding.

Here we see an echo of the representational complex exhibited in the ethnic maps and photographs from the 1935 Taiwan Expo: progress was being made among the indigenes, but they remained and would always remain a rural folk rooted to the land and engaged in useful pursuits, as members of cohesive, tradition-bound collectivities. Insofar as such a construction was a projection of Japanese conservative fantasies about the timeless virtues embodied in the imperiled and deracinated rural population of the home islands, it makes sense to view the indigenization of Taiwan’s interior as a concomitant of Japanese nation building.
zh: 松田这一总体主张的证据十分充足。其一，1890年代末至1910年代的原住民观光计划，是把少量头人与传统领袖带到日本城市，通过展示日军装备与本土先进基础设施来吓唬他们归顺；而1930年代的参观，则涉及从原住民青年团组织来的大批团员，前往原住民领土内的示范农场，或台湾与日本其他繁荣的农业地点。目标不再是植入日本压倒性现代性与权力的图景，而是传授作物栽培和畜牧的实用知识。
这里我们看到1935年台湾博览会族群地图与照片共同表达的观念：原住民中正在取得进步，但他们仍然、并将永远是一个扎根土地、从事有用营生的乡村民众，作为凝聚的、受传统束缚的集体的成员。就这样一种建构是日本保守派幻想的投射——关于日本本土日益受威胁、日渐脱离原有生活根基的乡村人口所体现的永恒美德——而言，把台湾内陆的原住民化视为日本民族建构的伴随物，是说得通的。

en: More importantly, Taiwan-based academic, commercial, and official institutions had financial, emotional, and careerist stakes in the maintenance of the second-order geobody of the indigenous territory and its subdivision into ethnically defined language groups. Perhaps most prominent among them were the indigenous territory police and the aborigine youth corps that rose to prominence in the wake of the Wushe uprising. Both institutions were invested in the kind of modified preservationism described by Matsuda and had grown elaborate and cross-cutting organizational structures by the 1930s. The new youth leaders were fluent in Japanese, not Chinese. The lingua franca that linked them to other indigenous youth leaders separated them from Han Taiwanese, as it promoted sociability and identification with their indigenous police counterparts.
zh: 更重要的是，设于台湾的学术、商业与官方机构，在维持原住民领土这个二阶地理体，以及按族群将其进一步划分为不同语言群体，都牵涉财政、情感与职业上的利益。其中或许最突出的，是雾社起义后崛起的蕃地警察与蕃人青年团。这两个机构都投入于松田所描述的那种修正版保存主义，到1930年代已发展出复杂、彼此交叠的组织结构。新一代青年领袖流利的是日语，而非汉语。把他们与其他原住民青年领袖联系起来的通用语，把他们与台湾汉人隔开，因为它促进了与原住民警察同侪的社交与认同。

en: The interests of the indigenous police bureaucracy dovetailed with local boosters who lobbied for the selection of Taroko and Alishan National Parks above other sites in Taiwan. This group included primitivists like Lan Yinding and Ōzaki Hotsuma, Japanese alpinists, ethnologists at Taihoku Imperial University, musicologist Kurosawa Takatomo, and the many Japanese tourists, consumers, and collectors who were emotionally invested in the continued existence of Taiwan Indigenous Peoples as an identifiably separate and autochthonous population.
zh: 蕃地警务系统的利益，与地方推动者的利益不谋而合——后者游说优先选定太鲁阁和阿里山作为国家公园用地。这一群体包括蓝荫鼎（Lan Yinding）与尾崎秀真（Ōzaki Hotsuma）这样的原始主义者、日本登山家、台北帝国大学的民族学家、音乐学家黑泽隆朝（Kurosawa Takatomo），以及众多希望台湾原住民作为可辨识、有独立身份且植根本地的群体继续存在，并对此抱有情感寄托的日本游客、消费者与收藏家。

en: To summarize, this book has considered the emergence of indigenous modernity as a two-part invention. The first part is a combination of military force sufficient to rob peoples in dynastic-state peripheries of their autonomy, coupled with an insufficiency of state resources to create disciplinary societies. In areas of Taiwan not already softened up by Chinese immigration and Qing governance, punishment remained ascendant over discipline into the 1930s. Here, it is important to consider the fact that the GMD itself, with many more resources, maintained the ethnically bifurcated form of rule in Taiwan. Its historical resilience indicates that “specially administered territory” is more than a residual category. Rather, these homelands embody positivities that gained considerable historical inertia during a moment in world-historical time marked by the ascendance of cultural pluralism.
zh: 总而言之，本书把原住民现代性的浮现视为一部由两部分构成的创意曲（two-part invention）。第一部分是如下两者的结合：足以剥夺王朝国家边缘各民族自主性的军事力量，加上国家资源不足以创造规训社会。在台湾那些尚未受过汉人移民和清朝治理预先影响的地区，直到1930年代，惩罚仍比规训占更重要的位置。这里，重要的是考虑这一事实：国民党本身拥有更多资源，却维持了台湾族群二分的统治形式。其历史韧性表明，“特别行政区”不止是一个残余类别。相反，在文化多元主义兴起的世界历史阶段，这些原住民家园也形成了持久的文化与制度内容，并延续了下来。

en: These positivities sank roots in Taiwan coterminously with the so-called “cultural policy” in Korea, in tandem with a more diffuse, Wilsonian world order that moved sovereignty from an achieved status (civilized nations only) toward an ascribed status (all nations are ipso facto sovereign). The second part of this invention is then the construction of the second-order geobodies that formed the bulwarks of cultural pluralism in colonized Taiwan. As we have seen, the artistic, commercial, and scholarly impulses to collect, preserve, and idealize elements of indigenous cultures produced reified versions of them in museum collections, postcards, folklore anthologies, and ethnographic portraits. These preserved versions of indigenous culture have been sources of contestation, while they have also been utilized as resources for indigenous survival. The extent to which certain taxonomies, ethnonyms, or other articulations of indigenous culture are Japanese inventions is debatable. However, the shape and fundamental nature of the second-order geobody is not. It was under Japanese colonial rule that polygons such as the one illustrated in
were consolidated.
zh: 这些文化与制度成果在台湾扎根，与朝鲜所谓“文化政策”同期，也与威尔逊式世界秩序在更广范围内的扩展同步——后者把主权从一种须满足条件才能取得的地位（仅限被认定为“文明”的国家）移向一种与生俱来的地位，即每个民族都因其为民族而拥有主权（ipso facto）。这项发明的第二部分，则是二阶地理体的建构，它们构成了被殖民台湾文化多元主义的堡垒。如我们所见，收集、保存与理想化原住民文化要素的艺术、商业与学术冲动，在博物馆收藏、明信片、民俗选集与民族志肖像中，把流动的文化要素呈现为固定、可观察的形态。这些被保存的原住民文化版本一直是争议的源头，同时也被用作原住民生存的资源。某些分类法、族名或原住民文化的其他表述在多大程度上是日本的发明，是可争议的。然而，二阶地理体的形状与根本性质却不容争议。正是在日本殖民统治下，
所示那类多边形才得以确立。

en: Over the course of its rule, the Taiwan Government-General zoned most of

country as public land, save for a small percentage reserved for villages and their residents. This process amounted to land confiscation. Ownership of public lands was transferred to the GMD after retrocession in 1945. While the lands that were taken away from indigenes during the camphor wars and subsequent dispossession operations from 1898 through the 1930s were inhabited by myriad settlements and distinct collectivities then known as Gaogan, Dakekan, Nan’ao, or Tgdaya peoples, litigation with Taiwan’s central government now aims to recover an Atayal homeland. In their analysis of the struggles surrounding the establishment of Maqaw National Park in north-central Taiwan, activist-scholars Yih-ren Lin, Lahuy Icyeh, and Da-Wei Kuan have argued that its proposed boundaries fall squarely within “Atayal people’s traditional territory.” The map they use to make this argument depicts Maqaw National Park enveloped by a much larger Atayal homeland. The space demarcated as territory to be restored to Atayal management, if not sovereignty, is not the home of a particular dialect community, ritual group, or voting district but rather is none other than the one drawn up by Japanese ethnologists, as shown in
zh: 在其统治过程中，台湾总督府把大部分泰雅地域划为公有土地，只留一小部分给村落及其居民。这一过程无异于土地没收。1945年台湾由中华民国接管后，公有土地所有权移交给国民党政府。虽然从1898年到1930年代樟脑战争及随后剥夺行动中从原住民手里夺走的土地，当时居住着无数聚落与当时被称为高干、大嵙崁、南澳或德固达雅人的不同集体，如今与台湾中央政府的诉讼却旨在收复一片泰雅家园。兼具倡议者身份的学者林益仁（Yih-ren Lin）、拉互伊·伊界（Lahuy Icyeh）与官大伟（Da-Wei Kuan）在分析台湾中北部马告（Maqaw）国家公园设立前后的斗争时论证道，其拟议边界恰恰落在“泰雅族人的传统领域”之内。他们用以论证的地图，描绘马告国家公园被一片大得多的泰雅家园所环绕。在图上划出、主张应归还泰雅人管理的地域，即使归还的未必是主权，不是某个特定方言社群、仪式群体或选区的家园，而恰恰是日本民族学家所绘制的那一个，如

en: There are many good practical, historical, and legal reasons to consider this land as Atayal and for the central government to comanage public lands with Atayal people. There is no other effective way to configure autonomy, sovereignty, and rights in land nowadays, except territorially. The architects of the Japanese colonial project in ethnic bifurcation, who were many and not exactly in cahoots, did not predetermine how these thorny problems will be resolved. But this study suggests that they set the terms of engagement.
zh: 有许多充分的实务、历史与法律理由，把这片土地视为泰雅传统领地，并让中央政府与泰雅人共管公有土地。如今，要有效安排自治、主权和土地权利，唯一可行的办法是明确其适用的领土范围。日本殖民时期促成台湾族群二分的人为数众多，彼此间也谈不上统一策划，他们并未预先决定这些棘手问题将如何解决。但本研究表明，他们奠定了此后交涉所依据的基本框架。
